svg.title: Parabolic bundle atlas and an obstructed line reduction
svg.desc: SG.1–SG.4 construct the atlas using projective Hilbert graphs. SG.5–SG.9 describe relative deformations, the nilradical cone and isotropy. SG.10–SG.14 give an SL2 square-zero bundle deformation with no lifted positive-degree line reduction.
svg.text: A parabolic atlas and a relative obstruction
Any parabolic of a connected reductive group · every genus · arbitrary coefficient tests
1. The section scheme from Hilbert graphs (SG.1–SG.3)
Y = P/Q ↪ Fl(ad P) over X_T; T ×_{Bun_G} Bun_Q = Sec(Y/X_T)
H = ⨿ Hilbᵖ(Y/T); universal flat D → X_H is projective.
Near a graph: finite projection; unit O_{X_H} → a_* O_D becomes an isomorphism.
The open graph locus is Sec(Y/X_T). Finite coordinate data carry it to all test rings.
2. The cartesian atlas (SG.4)
V_Q = V ×_{Bun_G} Bun_Q
V
Bun_Q
Bun_G
smooth atlas
smooth atlas
Both vertical maps are smooth; no smoothness of the horizontal maps is assumed.
3. Tangent, nilradical parameters and chart isotropy (SG.5–SG.9)
T Bun_Q = RΓ(q_P)[1]; T_f = RΓ((g/q)_P)
H⁰(T_f): reduction deformations; H¹(T_f): their obstructions
C_F = ker(K⁰ → K¹), affine of finite presentation, even when section ranks jump
A dense-open reduction lifts tangent vectors: λ_A|W₀ = 0 ⇒ W isotropic ⇒ dim W ≤ dim A
4. An exact SL₂ deformation with no lifted line (SG.10–SG.14)
X = ℙ¹; E = O(1) ⊕ O(−1); B preserves the first line; ε² = 0
g₀∞ = [ z 0 ; ε z⁻¹ ], det(g₀∞) = 1
A lifted line forces z⁻¹ = a₀(z) − z⁻² a∞(z⁻¹).
Allowed exponents on the right: ≥ 0 or ≤ −2. The required exponent −1 is absent.
Bun_B: (h⁰,h¹) = (4,0), dimension −4
Bun_SL₂: (h⁰,h¹) = (4,1), dimension −3; relative obstruction H¹(O(−2)) = k
The nilradical Higgs fibre is H⁰(O(2) ⊗ ω_ℙ¹) = k.
Proof and solved exercises: §§6.3.1–6.3.2, SG.1–SG.14, Exercises6.J–6.L.
Free human comparison for the graph locus: Stacks Project, Tags 0D1A–0D1B.
